findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the Approach claim: say POSIX behaviour is unchanged on UTF-8 locales except at sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py, which deliberately switch to errors="replace" for arbitrary file content.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:104-111: subprocess.run([... 'grep' ...], text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", check=False)
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:216-223: subprocess.run([... 'show', f'HEAD:{path}'], text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", check=False)
Approach: 'Add encoding="utf-8" to each of the 85 calls, keeping any errors= the call already passes' and 'strict decoding ... keeps that equivalence'
The claim that the POSIX locale codec is always UTF-8 is an environment fact the tools can't check. A non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. ISO-8859-1) would also break the equivalence.
findings.finding: The Approach says naming UTF-8 with strict decoding 'leaves POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged'. The plan's own Scope addition breaks this. sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py now decode with errors="replace", which those calls did not pass before, so on POSIX invalid bytes are now replaced instead of raising. The Approach paragraph was not updated to reflect this.
findings.location: Approach ("naming UTF-8 leaves POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged ... strict decoding (rather than errors="replace") keeps that equivalence") vs Scope ("Added during review: ... sunset_markers.py and ... engine_comparison.py ... decode with errors=\"replace\"")
scenarios: A repo file containing non-UTF-8 bytes: before the change, `git grep`/`git show` on POSIX raised UnicodeDecodeError; after it, they silently produce U+FFFD output. That is a POSIX behaviour change the Approach says cannot happen.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, after 'strict decoding ... keeps that equivalence', add: 'Exception: the two review-added sites that read arbitrary repository content (sunset_markers.py `git grep`, engine_comparison.py `git show`) pass errors="replace" on purpose, so on POSIX they now replace undecodable bytes instead of raising.' Also limit the equivalence claim to UTF-8 POSIX locales.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Amend the Approach to state the errors="replace" exception and its selection rule (sites decoding arbitrary repository file content), and list every site it applies to.
evidence: Approach: 'strict decoding (rather than `errors="replace"`) keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output instead of masking it'

Scope: '`src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py` and `src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py` (`git grep`/`git show` of arbitrary file content decode with `errors="replace"`, an LLM-Review advisory)'
findings.finding: Approach and Scope conflict on how errors are handled. Approach mandates strict decoding: 'strict decoding (rather than errors="replace") keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output', and only 'keeping any errors= the call already passes'. Scope's review addendum adds errors="replace" to the git grep/git show reads in sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py. The Approach never states this exception or the rule that decides which sites get it.
scenarios: An implementer following the Approach leaves these two sites strict, or applies errors="replace" to other git-show-of-file-content sites, such as verify_commit or repo_snapshot, inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach: 'Exception: calls whose stdout is arbitrary repository file content (git grep, git show <rev>:<path>), currently sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py, also pass errors="replace", because tracked files need not be UTF-8. All other sites decode strictly.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Label the `errors="replace"` hunks in `sunset_markers.py` and `engine_comparison.py` as an intentional in-scope exception (with the reason lenient decoding suits arbitrary file content), and qualify the Approach's 'POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged' claim to exclude them.
evidence: Approach: "Add `encoding=\"utf-8\"` to each of the 85 calls, keeping any `errors=` the call already passes... naming UTF-8 leaves POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged... strict decoding (rather than `errors=\"replace\"`) keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output instead of masking it."
Scope: "`git grep`/`git show` of arbitrary file content decode with `errors=\"replace\"`, an LLM-Review advisory"
Code: `sunset_markers.py:104-110` and `engine_comparison.py:216-222` pass `text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`.
findings.finding: The review-added hunks in `src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py` and `src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py` add `errors="replace"`, a behaviour change that contradicts the Approach. The plan records them as an 'LLM-Review advisory' but does not classify them as a deliberate in-scope change, and does not reconcile them with the strict-decoding rationale.
scenarios: On Linux, `git grep`/`git show` output containing invalid UTF-8 used to raise `UnicodeDecodeError` and now silently becomes U+FFFD. That changes POSIX behaviour, which the Approach says will not happen.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, add: "Exception: `sunset_markers.py` (`git grep`) and `engine_comparison.py` (`git show HEAD:<path>`) read arbitrary repository file content and use `errors=\"replace\"`; on POSIX this turns invalid-UTF-8 bytes into U+FFFD where a strict decode would raise, which is intentional for these scanners."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rule for strict vs `errors="replace"` (e.g. replace for any site that decodes arbitrary repository file content, strict for structured/metadata output), apply it to every content-reading site (diff/blob/grep), and correct the 'every child writes UTF-8' claim.
evidence: Approach: 'Every child these sites start (git, gh, ssh-keygen, ...) writes UTF-8 or ASCII.'
Approach: 'strict decoding (rather than `errors="replace"`) keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output instead of masking it.'
Scope: '`git grep`/`git show` of arbitrary file content decode with `errors="replace"`, an LLM-Review advisory'
No statement classifying the remaining 80+ sites by whether they read arbitrary file content.
findings.finding: The Approach says every child writes UTF-8 or ASCII and that strict decoding is the policy. The Scope addition contradicts this: `sunset_markers.py` and `engine_comparison.py` decode `git grep`/`git show` of arbitrary file content with errors="replace". The plan never states the rule for when a site gets strict versus replace. It also never audits the other sites that read repository content (diffs, blobs, grep output), e.g. `footprint.py`, `commit_impact.py` and `repo_snapshot.py`. On Windows those sites change from cp1252, which decodes almost any byte, to strict UTF-8, which raises UnicodeDecodeError on non-UTF-8 file bytes. That is a new failure disposition on Windows with no stated caller outcome.
findings.location: Approach ('Every child these sites start ... writes UTF-8 or ASCII'; 'strict decoding ... surfaces corrupt output') vs Scope ('Added during review: ... `git grep`/`git show` of arbitrary file content decode with `errors="replace"`')
scenarios: On Windows, a diff or `git show` of a Latin-1 or binary-ish tracked file decoded through a strict site used to garble under cp1252. It now raises UnicodeDecodeError and aborts the command.
A future content-reading site copies the strict pattern because the plan's stated rule says all git output is UTF-8.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach: 'Sites whose output includes arbitrary tracked-file content (git diff/show/grep of blobs) use encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"; metadata/structured output stays strict.' Then list which of the 85 sites fall in each class.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default in the scan rule: on subprocess.* callees, any text/universal_newlines keyword that is not the literal False counts as text mode; add a parametrized case for a non-literal text= value.
evidence: 'run a child in text mode (`text=`/`universal_newlines=` not literally false)'
'flag a call when it has a truthy `text`/`universal_newlines` keyword'
findings.finding: The guard's text-mode test is worded two ways. The Census counts calls where text/universal_newlines is 'not literally false'. The scan rule flags 'a truthy text/universal_newlines keyword'. For non-literal values such as text=capture or text=kwargs.get(...), 'truthy' cannot be decided statically, so it is unclear whether the guard flags those subprocess calls.
scenarios: The guard is written to accept only literal True on subprocess.* callees and misses a call like subprocess.run(..., text=as_text). The tree-wide guarantee then quietly has a hole.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the rule: 'flag a call when it has a text/universal_newlines keyword whose value is not the literal False, and no encoding keyword, and either its callee is subprocess.<run|Popen|check_output|check_call|call> or the text keyword is the literal True.' Add a synthetic case `subprocess.run(cmd, text=flag)` that must be flagged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate the UTF-8 output assumption for the non-git Windows-native children (ssh-keygen, docker, acli, gh) on the Windows sweep, or decode their stderr with errors="replace" and say so in the Approach.
evidence: 'Every child these sites start (git, gh, ssh-keygen, ruff, uv, docker, acli, jscpd, the rebar CLI itself) writes UTF-8 or ASCII.'
Testing lists only the AST guard and make verify; there is no Windows run of a stderr-producing failure path.
findings.finding: The claim that every child writes UTF-8 or ASCII is asserted, not checked on Windows. Strict UTF-8 replaces cp1252, which leaves only 5 byte values undefined. Any non-UTF-8 byte in captured stdout or stderr now raises UnicodeDecodeError from subprocess.run. Windows-native tools (ssh-keygen, docker, acli, gh) can emit localized error text in the OEM/ANSI codepage. On those error paths the decode error is raised inside communicate(), before the caller's returncode or CalledProcessError handling runs, so the real failure message is replaced by a decode traceback. The plan's only proving step is a Linux-gate AST scan, which cannot reveal this.
findings.location: Approach ('Every child these sites start ... writes UTF-8 or ASCII'; strict decoding rationale)
scenarios: On a localized Windows host, ssh-keygen or docker fails with an accented error message in cp1252. The new strict decode raises UnicodeDecodeError, and the caller's error branch never sees returncode or stderr.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the tree-wide guard on `tests/_tree_scan.parsed_python_files(REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar")`, not a hand-rolled `rglob` + `read_text` + `ast.parse` walk.
evidence: tests/_tree_scan.py:28-42: `@functools.cache def parsed_python_files(root)` — 'Return every *.py under root parsed once (cached per process)… callers that spell the same directory differently (`_SRC` vs `REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar"`) share one parse.'

tests/unit/test_no_bare_rebar_subprocess.py:20,94: `from _tree_scan import parsed_python_files` … `modules = parsed_python_files(_TESTS_ROOT)`. This is the existing pattern for an AST subprocess-call guard.

tests/unit/test_windows_text_encoding.py:140,181-182: `ast.walk(ast.parse(source))` and `sorted((REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar").rglob("*.py"))` / `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`. This builds the same walk again.
search for `from _tree_scan import` under tests/ returns about 37 importers (e.g. test_ruff_ratchet.py, test_spawn_detached.py, test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py).
findings.finding: The plan's tree-wide guard walks and parses `src/rebar` itself (`sorted((REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar").rglob("*.py"))` + `path.read_text(...)` + `ast.parse` inside `_locale_decoded_text_calls`). The repo already has a shared helper for exactly this: `tests/_tree_scan.parsed_python_files(root)`, which returns each module parsed once and caches the result per worker. It is used by about 37 policy tests, including the sibling subprocess guard `tests/unit/test_no_bare_rebar_subprocess.py`. The plan doesn't mention this helper, so the guard re-reads and re-parses about 1k source files that other src-tree oracles in the same worker have already parsed.
findings.location: Approach — 'a tree-wide test applying the scan rule above to every module under `src/rebar`'; tests/unit/test_windows_text_encoding.py:128-184
scenarios: The unit tier runs this guard in the same xdist worker as other src-tree oracles, and `src/rebar` is parsed one extra time per worker.
A later change to how policy scans discover files (e.g. excluding generated modules) is made in `_tree_scan` and silently skips this guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `_locale_decoded_text_calls` take an `ast.AST` instead of a source string. In the parametrized synthetic-snippet test, pass `ast.parse(source)`. In `test_no_src_call_decodes_child_output_with_the_locale_codec`, iterate `for module in parsed_python_files(REPO_ROOT / "src" / "rebar")` and report `f"{module.relative.as_posix()}:{line}"`, the same way `test_no_bare_rebar_subprocess.py` does.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ## Approach, state the rule for errors="replace": calls that decode arbitrary repository file content (git show <rev>:<path>, git grep) use errors="replace"; calls that read git metadata or tool output stay strict. Name sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py as the sites that follow it.
evidence: Approach: "Add encoding=\"utf-8\" to each of the 85 calls, keeping any errors= the call already passes ... strict decoding (rather than errors=\"replace\") keeps that equivalence"
Scope: "src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py and src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py (git grep/git show of arbitrary file content decode with errors=\"replace\", an LLM-Review advisory)"
src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:109 and src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:221 both pass errors="replace"
findings.finding: The Approach says every call keeps strict UTF-8 decoding ("strict decoding (rather than errors=\"replace\") keeps that equivalence"). Scope, however, adds errors="replace" to sunset_markers.py and engine_comparison.py because they decode arbitrary file content. The plan never states the rule for when a site gets errors="replace" instead of strict decoding, so the Approach and the actual change disagree, and nothing tells an implementer how to judge other sites that read arbitrary content.
findings.location: ## Approach (strict-decoding rationale) vs ## Scope ("Added during review")
scenarios: An implementer or later reviewer judging a new `git show <rev>:<path>` or `git grep` call has no stated rule for choosing strict or replace.
A reader of the Approach believes every edited call is strict and is surprised by the two replace sites.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to ## Approach: "Exception: calls that decode arbitrary repository file content (`git show <rev>:<path>`, `git grep`), which need not be UTF-8, also pass `errors=\"replace\"` (sunset_markers.py, engine_comparison.py); every other site decodes strictly."
